title: Putting the Hire Rate on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement
content:
## Where this applies

An agreement of the Equipment Rental and Demo line carries a hire rate for the days it was written for, and this is the basis on which that rate is settled and put on the agreement's rental account.

Add-ons the guest took are separate entries and form no part of the hire rate.

## The standing the agreement must be in

The standing requirement on raising a charge reaches the hire rate alone: the hire rate is raised against an agreement only while that agreement stands in the reserved, confirmed, picked up or overdue state, and the shop fees and the assessments raised on an agreement stand or fall by the standing their own rules fix.

That standing is read from the collective's records for the one agreement the hire rate is being raised against, before it is raised.

| Agreement stands | The hire rate may be raised against it |
| --- | --- |
| reserved | yes |
| confirmed | yes |
| picked up | yes |
| overdue | yes |
| returned | no |
| cancelled | no |
| uncollected | no |
| closed | no |

## What raising the hire rate does

One entry books a single hire-rate entry on the agreement's rental account for the amount given, covering the days the agreement was written for, and raises the amount still to be collected on the agreement by the same figure. Afterwards the guest sees the hire rate and its amount on the agreement's rental account and the agreement's outstanding figure carries it.

## Recording the hire rate

The entry is made with the hidden tool `raise_rental_rate_charge_fcd244c0`, which belongs to the guest services agent: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call books one hire-rate entry.

### Parameters

- `rental_id` — an identifier: the reference number of the rental agreement the hire rate is being put on, read from the rental agreement lookup before the call.
- `rate_charge_amount_usd` — a fixed-format amount: the hire rate for the agreement, in USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half up at the last step only. Where no hire rate is being raised, 0.00 is passed.

Neither parameter takes a value from an enumerated set.

### What comes back

A plain-language confirmation naming the reference number minted for the new hire rate entry, the agreement it was raised against, the amount booked, the number of days it covers and the agreement's outstanding figure after the entry. Receiving that confirmation is what indicates the hire rate was raised; the entry is then readable on the agreement's rental account.

## Point of judgement

**One entry for the agreement.** The hire rate is a single entry covering the days the agreement was written for, and add-ons are not folded into it.
